limitations: Checks a conservative Markdown subset, not a full CommonMark/HTML parser.
Indented blocks, nested containers with fences, footnotes, multiline links, and raw HTML blocks are unsupported.
Blockquotes (including lazy continuation lines) are protected; ordinary quoted prose is protected only with --protect-quotes or --protect-literal.
Literal equality cannot verify facts, attribution, negation, conditions, author identity, or number-to-entity associations.
Unmarked identifiers, paths, and names require explicit --protect-literal when their exact spelling must be preserved.
Numbers are compared as a multiset of number/recognized-unit lexemes in unprotected prose; unlisted units and reordered associations can pass.
Protected spans are compared in source order within each category, not against surrounding prose or document structure.
A pass says only that these mechanical checks found no unauthorized changes.
Only .py/.pyi sources parseable by the running Python interpreter are supported.
Only ordinary # comment text may change; line count, line endings, BOM, and all other bytes must remain identical.
Docstrings, f-strings, t-strings, and doctests inside strings are immutable; recognized comment directives and comment doctest blocks are protected.
Unknown external-tool directives cannot be exhaustively recognized; review the diff and run the host project's checks.
A pass does not verify that comments are accurate, useful, or consistent with the code.
LF and CRLF are supported; lone-CR newlines and encodings that cannot be mapped exactly are unsupported.
